item.title: What Nigeria Stocks Tell Investors About Africa Markets: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about Nigeria’s world-beating stocks, and where investors are finding opportunities in African markets, in a Live Q&A on Friday, July 17 at 12 p.m. GMT

item.title: Faena Condo Project Sells $30 Million Penthouse on Miami River
item.description: Argentine fashion entrepreneur-turned-developer Alan Faena sold a $30 million penthouse in his planned twin condo towers on the Miami River, a milestone in the mission to take his maximalist, theatrical brand worldwide.

item.title: Chile Senate Hands Kast a Win on Key Economic Reform Bill
item.description: Chile’s Senate gave its approval to President José Antonio Kast’s wide-ranging economic bill, clearing a key hurdle for an administration trying to revive the sluggish economy.

item.title: Citigroup Sees Bondholders Recover 50% of Senegal’s Debt Under Revamp
item.description: Holders of Senegal’s dollar bonds could end up recouping less than 50% of the face value of the securities in the event of a restructuring — below the prices at which the debt currently trades, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: Canada’s Forgotten Shale Gas Play Reemerges as Oil Hot Spot
item.description: On the edge of the Canadian Rocky Mountains, companies including Obsidian Energy Ltd. and Yangarra Resources Corp. are breathing new life into a long-dormant gas reservoir — except now they’re drilling for oil.

item.title: German Chemical Industry in Crisis Despite Reprieve, Lobby Says
item.description: Germany’s chemical industry remains in a structural crisis despite a brief breather when the conflict in the Middle East triggered stockpiling and hit rivals in Asia harder, according to the industry’s VCI association.

item.title: US Homebuilder Sentiment Slips Again to Match Year’s Low
item.description: Confidence among US homebuilders dropped for a second month to the lowest level of the year, dragged lower by elevated borrowing costs and higher material and land prices.

item.title: Raiffeisen Clears Key Hurdle in €517 Million Bid for Addiko Bank
item.description: Raiffeisen Bank International AG reached a key milestone in its bid to acquire Addiko Bank AG after shareholders representing more than 55% tendered their shares, reaching the offer’s minimum threshold.

item.title: Gaming Bonds Lose Allure as Threat From Prediction Markets Grows
item.description: Investors increasingly see gaming bonds as a losing bet.

item.title: Hoisington, US Bond Bull for Decades, Turns Decidedly Bearish
item.description: Hoisington Investment Management Co., the bond manager known for its bullish stance on US Treasuries going back more than 30 years, has turned bearish.

item.title: Sea Drone Maker Saronic to Build New Shipyard in South Texas
item.description: An Austin-based technology startup whose maritime drones were used by the US military in combat for the first time this week plans to build a $3.2 billion shipyard in South Texas.

item.title: Apple Nears Launch of OLED iPad Mini; New iPad Air and Base iPad in 2027
item.description: Apple Inc. is preparing to introduce its biggest overhaul to the iPad mini in half a decade, giving new life to a product that’s popular with travelers and technology enthusiasts.

item.title: Why IPOs of Tiny Foreign Companies Have Vanished in US
item.description: Added scrutiny on foreign microcaps puts a damper on public debuts

item.title: Jump Trading Doubles Team to Ride Record Prediction Market Boom
item.description: As prediction markets draw record trading around events like the World Cup, Jump Trading Group is betting the once-niche contracts are becoming a lasting corner of Wall Street.

item.title: Travel Agency Platform Fora Valued at $1 Billion in New Funding
item.description: Fora, an online platform for travel agents, has raised $60 million in funding at a $1 billion valuation, with the goal of adding artificial intelligence tools to help travel advisers accelerate their businesses.

item.title: Hollywood Sci-Fi Lot Pitched as Site to Make Real Space-Age Weapons
item.description: Manhattan Beach Studios has been the site of filming for projects including Stars Wars: The Mandalorian, a TV series about a heavily armed bounty hunter in a galaxy far, far away.

item.title: US Jobless Claims Decline to 208,000, Below Forecasts
item.description: Applications for US unemployment benefits fell last week, suggesting the labor market remains stable.

item.title: US Retail Sales Rise Modestly as Consumers Spend Less on Gas
item.description: US retail sales rose modestly in June, dragged down by a drop in gas-station receipts that masked strong gains at some merchants.

item.title: US Stocks Tumble as TSMC Results Revive AI Spending Concerns
item.description: US stocks declined on Thursday as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s results failed to boost artificial-intelligence stocks and traders assessed a worsening situation in the Middle East.

item.title: Multistrat Hedge Fund Paloma to Cut Teams in Latest Pivot
item.description: Donald Sussman, the veteran behind Paloma Partners, is pivoting his long-standing multistrategy hedge fund to focus on fewer managers in which he has the highest conviction as the firm adjusts to a decline in assets over the past three years.

item.title: French Government Starts 2027 Budget Showdown With Spending Caps
item.description: France’s government proposed tight spending caps across most ministries in 2027, kicking off a budget debate entangled with the uncertainty of a presidential election.

item.title: SMBC Bolsters Global Sales and Trading Push With Macro Hire
item.description: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. hired Kunal Maini as international head of macro rates, bolstering efforts to expand its sales and trading franchise beyond its core Japanese market.

item.title: Google Must Give Gemini Rivals Equal Access to Android System, EU Says
item.description: Google faces a European Union directive to open up its Android operating system to artificial intelligence rivals for certain features and give search data to competing online engine providers.

item.title: Franklin Templeton Cuts AI Bets, Favors Chinese Internet Stocks
item.description: Franklin Templeton’s main emerging equity fund has scaled back on memory chipmakers’ shares after their huge rally, instead favoring Chinese internet names such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and Tencent Holdings Ltd.

item.title: US Drivers Are Again Paying More Than $5 a Gallon for Diesel
item.description: American drivers are once again paying more than $5 a gallon for diesel, with a fresh round of hostilities in the Middle East raising the specter of more war-induced inflation.

item.title: US Stock Futures Today: AtaiBeckley, GE Aerospace, UnitedHealth
item.description: S&P 500 Index futures are down 0.2% as of 7:47 a.m. in New York. The US intensified strikes against Iran, hitting an oil tanker near the country’s main export terminal for the first time since the restart of the blockade on the Islamic Republic’s ports.

item.title: CXMT’s Blockbuster IPO 212 Times Covered for Retail Investors
item.description: The marquee listing of CXMT Corp. ignited a rush among retail investors as China’s homegrown memory giant opened books for an initial public offering to raise $9.8 billion, the second-largest in the nation’s history.

item.title: Abbott Boosts 2026 Profit Guidance as Sales Across Business Rise
item.description: Abbott Laboratories raised its 2026 profit guidance after a stronger-than-expected second quarter driven by improved performance across most of its business lines.

item.title: US Power Grid Faces Defining Test for AI Boom
item.description: The operator of America’s biggest electricity network is entering an emergency process to plug a projected supply shortfall.

item.title: Retail Traders’ Rise Upends the Established Stock Market Order
item.description: Retail traders have moved from the stock market’s margins to its center.
